# NYC Motor Vehicle Collisions — Crashes

Source: NYC Open Data, dataset `h9gi-nx95` ("Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes"), published by the NYPD. Snapshot downloaded 2026-10-03.

Official description (paraphrased): each row is one police-reported motor vehicle collision in New York City. A police report (MV-104AN) is required when someone is injured or killed, or when there is at least $1,000 of damage. The data is preliminary and subject to change.

File: `crashes.parquet` (one row per crash)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| collision_id | BIGINT | Unique identifier of the crash |
| crash_date | DATE | Date of the crash |
| crash_time | TIME | Time of the crash |
| borough | VARCHAR | Borough where the crash occurred |
| zip_code | VARCHAR | Postal code of the crash location |
| latitude, longitude | DOUBLE | Coordinates of the crash location |
| location | VARCHAR | Latitude/longitude pair |
| on_street_name | VARCHAR | Street on which the crash occurred |
| cross_street_name | VARCHAR | Nearest cross street |
| off_street_name | VARCHAR | Street address if known |

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_parquet('./data/crashes.parquet')
df['crash_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['crash_date'])
df['year'] = df['crash_date'].dt.year
df['month'] = df['crash_date'].dt.to_period('M')

# Annual cyclist injuries and fatalities
annual = df.groupby('year').agg(
    cyclist_injured=('number_of_cyclist_injured', 'sum'),
    cyclist_killed=('number_of_cyclist_killed', 'sum'),
    total_crashes=('collision_id', 'count')
).reset_index()

# Also calculate cyclist crashes (crashes involving at least 1 cyclist injured/killed)
cyclist_crashes = df[(df['number_of_cyclist_injured'] > 0) | (df['number_of_cyclist_killed'] > 0)]
annual_cyclist_crashes = cyclist_crashes.groupby('year').size().reset_index(name='cyclist_involved_crashes')

annual = annual.merge(annual_cyclist_crashes, on='year', how='left').fillna(0)

print(annual.to_string(index=False))
"

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_parquet('./data/crashes.parquet')
df['crash_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['crash_date'])
df['year'] = df['crash_date'].dt.year
df['month'] = df['crash_date'].dt.to_period('M')

# Full years only (2013-2025)
full_years = df[(df['year'] >= 2013) & (df['year'] <= 2025)]

annual = full_years.groupby('year').agg(
    cyclist_injured=('number_of_cyclist_injured', 'sum'),
    cyclist_killed=('number_of_cyclist_killed', 'sum'),
    total_crashes=('collision_id', 'count'),
    total_injured=('number_of_persons_injured', 'sum'),
    total_killed=('number_of_persons_killed', 'sum')
).reset_index()

cyclist_crashes = full_years[(full_years['number_of_cyclist_injured'] > 0) | (full_years['number_of_cyclist_killed'] > 0)]
annual_cyclist_crashes = cyclist_crashes.groupby('year').size().reset_index(name='cyclist_involved_crashes')

annual = annual.merge(annual_cyclist_crashes, on='year', how='left').fillna(0)

# Calculate rates
annual['cyclist_injured_per_1000_crashes'] = annual['cyclist_injured'] / annual['total_crashes'] * 1000
annual['cyclist_killed_per_1000_crashes'] = annual['cyclist_killed'] / annual['total_crashes'] * 1000
annual['cyclist_crashes_pct'] = annual['cyclist_involved_crashes'] / annual['total_crashes'] * 100

print(annual[['year', 'cyclist_injured', 'cyclist_killed', 'total_crashes', 'cyclist_involved_crashes', 
              'cyclist_injured_per_1000_crashes', 'cyclist_killed_per_1000_crashes', 'cyclist_crashes_pct']].to_string(index=False))
"

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_parquet('./data/crashes.parquet')
df['crash_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['crash_date'])
df['year'] = df['crash_date'].dt.year

full_years = df[(df['year'] >= 2013) & (df['year'] <= 2025)]

annual = full_years.groupby('year').agg(
    cyclist_injured=('number_of_cyclist_injured', 'sum'),
    cyclist_killed=('number_of_cyclist_killed', 'sum'),
    total_crashes=('collision_id', 'count')
).reset_index()

cyclist_crashes = full_years[(full_years['number_of_cyclist_injured'] > 0) | (full_years['number_of_cyclist_killed'] > 0)]
annual_cyclist_crashes = cyclist_crashes.groupby('year').size().reset_index(name='cyclist_involved_crashes')
annual = annual.merge(annual_cyclist_crashes, on='year', how='left').fillna(0)

annual['cyclist_injured_per_1000_crashes'] = annual['cyclist_injured'] / annual['total_crashes'] * 1000
annual['cyclist_killed_per_1000_crashes'] = annual['cyclist_killed'] / annual['total_crashes'] * 1000
annual['cyclist_crashes_pct'] = annual['cyclist_involved_crashes'] / annual['total_crashes'] * 100

# Create plots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# 1. Absolute cyclist injuries and fatalities
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
ax1.bar(annual['year'], annual['cyclist_injured'], alpha=0.7, label='Injured', color='steelblue')
ax1.set_ylabel('Cyclists Injured')
ax1.set_title('Cyclist Injuries per Year (Absolute)')
ax1.legend()
ax1.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

ax1b = ax1.twinx()
ax1b.plot(annual['year'], annual['cyclist_killed'], 'ro-', label='Killed', linewidth=2)
ax1b.set_ylabel('Cyclists Killed', color='red')
ax1b.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='red')
ax1b.legend(loc='upper right')

# 2. Total crashes vs cyclist-involved crashes
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
ax2.bar(annual['year'], annual['total_crashes'], alpha=0.5, label='All Crashes', color='gray')
ax2.bar(annual['year'], annual['cyclist_involved_crashes'], alpha=0.8, label='Cyclist-Involved', color='orange')
ax2.set_ylabel('Number of Crashes')
ax2.set_title('Total Crashes vs Cyclist-Involved Crashes')
ax2.legend()
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 3. Cyclist injuries per 1000 crashes (rate)
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
ax3.plot(annual['year'], annual['cyclist_injured_per_1000_crashes'], 'b-o', linewidth=2, markersize=6)
ax3.set_ylabel('Cyclist Injuries per 1,000 Crashes')
ax3.set_title('Cyclist Injury Rate (per 1,000 Total Crashes)')
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 4. Cyclist crashes as % of total
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
ax4.plot(annual['year'], annual['cyclist_crashes_pct'], 'g-o', linewidth=2, markersize=6)
ax4.set_ylabel('% of Crashes Involving Cyclists')
ax4.set_title('Cyclist-Involved Crashes as % of All Crashes')
ax4.grid(alpha=0.3)

for ax in axes.flat:
    ax.set_xlabel('Year')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('./out/cyclist_safety_trends.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print('Saved chart to ./out/cyclist_safety_trends.png')
"

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_parquet('./data/crashes.parquet')
df['crash_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['crash_date'])
df['year_month'] = df['crash_date'].dt.to_period('M')

# Monthly cyclist injuries
monthly = df.groupby('year_month').agg(
    cyclist_injured=('number_of_cyclist_injured', 'sum'),
    cyclist_killed=('number_of_cyclist_killed', 'sum'),
    total_crashes=('collision_id', 'count')
).reset_index()

monthly['year_month_dt'] = monthly['year_month'].dt.to_timestamp()
monthly['cyclist_injured_per_1000'] = monthly['cyclist_injured'] / monthly['total_crashes'] * 1000

# Plot monthly trends
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(14, 8))

ax1 = axes[0]
ax1.plot(monthly['year_month_dt'], monthly['cyclist_injured'], alpha=0.6, label='Monthly')
# 12-month rolling average
monthly['injured_rolling'] = monthly['cyclist_injured'].rolling(12, center=True).mean()
ax1.plot(monthly['year_month_dt'], monthly['injured_rolling'], 'r-', linewidth=2, label='12-month rolling avg')
ax1.set_ylabel('Cyclists Injured')
ax1.set_title('Monthly Cyclist Injuries with 12-Month Rolling Average')
ax1.legend()
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

ax2 = axes[1]
ax2.plot(monthly['year_month_dt'], monthly['cyclist_injured_per_1000'], alpha=0.6, label='Monthly rate')
monthly['rate_rolling'] = monthly['cyclist_injured_per_1000'].rolling(12, center=True).mean()

part.text:
Based on the NYC motor vehicle collision data (2013–2025), **cyclists are not safer in NYC than they used to be** — by several key measures, the risk has increased substantially.

## Key Findings

| Metric | Pre-COVID (2013–2019) | Post-COVID (2021–2025) | Change |
|--------|----------------------|------------------------|--------|
| Total crashes | 1,531,386 | 487,914 | **-68%** |
| Cyclists injured | 31,935 | 25,675 | -20% (but over shorter period) |
| Cyclists killed | 132 | 116 | similar |
| **Injury rate (per 1,000 crashes)** | **20.9** | **52.6** | **+152%** |
| **% of crashes involving cyclists** | **2.1%** | **5.2%** | **+148%** |

## What the charts show

**`./out/cyclist_safety_trends.png`** — Four-panel view:
- Absolute injuries stayed ~4,000–5,300/year, but total crashes plummeted from ~230K to ~85K
- Cyclist injury rate per 1,000 crashes **tripled** from ~20 to ~60
- Cyclist-involved crashes grew from ~2% to ~6% of all crashes

**`./out/cyclist_monthly_trends.png`** — Monthly detail with 12-month rolling averages showing the sustained elevation post-2020.

## Interpretation

Total crashes dropped dramatically (likely due to reduced driving during/after COVID, reporting changes, and Vision Zero interventions), but **cyclist crashes did not decline proportionally**. A cyclist's share of the collision burden has more than doubled. Without data on cycling volumes (miles traveled), we can't compute a true exposure-based rate, but the collision-data perspective is clear: **cyclists represent a growing fraction of NYC's traffic safety problem**.
